prompts.text: Name a national capital city that starts with B

items.quip: Founded by the French in 1627, its name just means lowland.
items.title: Basseterre
items.description: Capital city of Saint Kitts and Nevis
items.extract: Basseterre is the capital and largest city of Saint Kitts and Nevis with an estimated population of 14,000 in 2018. Geographically, the Basseterre port is located at 17°18′N 62°44′W, on the south-western coast of Saint Kitts Island, and it is one of the chief commercial depots of the Leeward Islands. The city lies within Saint George Basseterre Parish.

prompts.text: Name a mammal or reptile that lives in the desert

items.quip: Blind and earless, it swims through Australian sand.
items.title: Marsupial mole
items.extract:
Marsupial moles, from the genus Notoryctes are two species of highly specialized marsupial mammals that are found in the Australian interior. 
They are small burrowing marsupials that anatomically converge on fossorial placental mammals, such as extant golden moles (Chrysochloridae) and extinct epoicotheres. The species are:Notoryctes typhlops 
Notoryctes caurinus

items.quip: Sidewinds the Namib and drinks fog straight off its scales.
items.title: Bitis peringueyi
items.extract: Bitis peringueyi, also known as the Peringuey's adder, Peringuey's desert adder or desert sidewinding adder, is a viper species found in Namibia and southern Angola. No subspecies are currently recognized.

prompts.text: Name a type of cookie (brands don't count)

items.quip: New Mexico made it America's first official state cookie in 1989.
items.title: Bizcochito
items.extract: The bizcochito or biscochito is a New Mexican crisp butter cookie made with lard, flavored with sugar, cinnamon, and anise. The dough is rolled thin and cut into the shape of the fleur-de-lis, the Christian cross, a star, or a circle, symbolizing the moon.

items.quip: British kids call this currant biscuit the squashed fly biscuit.
items.title: Garibaldi biscuit
items.description: British rectangular biscuit with a middle layer of currants
items.extract: The Garibaldi biscuit consists of currants squashed and sandwiched between two thin oblongs of biscuit dough before baking. The biscuits are similar to Eccles cake.

items.quip: Monk's cashier in 101 episodes, and almost never a line.
items.title: Ruth Cohen (actress)
items.extract: Ruth Cohen was an American character actress who worked primarily as an extra on television sitcoms. She is best known for her recurring role as a cashier on the NBC sitcom Seinfeld (1992–1998).

items.description: Field of study in explosive materials
items.extract: Explosives engineering is the field of science and engineering which is related to examining the behavior and usage of explosive materials.

items.quip: Shoe sizes still step up by one third-inch barleycorn.
items.title: Barleycorn (unit)
items.description: Historic unit of length, basis of shoe sizes
items.extract: The barleycorn is an English unit of length equal to 1⁄3 of an inch. It is still used as the basis of shoe sizes in some English-speaking countries.

items.quip: Twelve numbered beads doctors hold against testicles to size them.
items.title: Orchidometer
items.extract: An orchidometer is a medical instrument used to measure the volume of the testicles.

items.quip: Small plate doctors tapped on the chest to sound out lungs.
items.title: Pleximeter
items.extract: A Pleximeter is a device used in medical percussion, as part of a clinical examination, to absorb the energy generated by the strike from the plexor.
